title: Does anyone still find King Kong (2005) to be a flawed masterpiece and one of the greatest action/adventure films ever made?

commenti.body:
It is very interesting to see this in hindsight after all the superhero movies and stuff like Avatar turned 2.5 hours into a base line. Kong is overstuffed but it maybe doesn’t feel as drawn out now as it did before. And you are absolutely right that however “too” much there is there is all superbly done. 

In the context of Jackson I do think it looks of a kind with the Hobbit films. A great craftsman who doesn’t know when to reign it is. And maybe that is his whole career but budget limits provided the reigns before. The downside is The Hobbit but the upside is Lord of the Rings probably isn’t what it is without someone going so big and so hard. 

There are fan edits of Kong that “improve” it as a movie but I’m not sure exactly that they’re better. In some sense the entire point of this Kong is excess. A dinosaur swinging in a vine is the soul of the film. And with home viewing it can be taken at a more leisurely pace.

I grew up loving this movie as a kid. It wasn’t until a few years ago that I watched it with adult eyes and I gotta say there’s more to love than hate in it. Yeah it could be tighter runtime wise but ultimately I think it did exactly what it was trying to do and it did it well. The Skull Island stuff alone makes this well worth the watch.

It was the longest movie I had seen when I first watched it at 11. I don’t think I had ever seen something with such a scale to it. It truly felt like my first epic. Also, King Kong fatality-ing a fucking T-Rex will never NOT be cool for a boy

Its a mixed-bag, but the overall effect is very strong. The film is overlong - Jackson things so too - and fragmented. The early scenes on the boat are a waste of time, when we get the island it feels like the adventures of the men looking after Anne takes precedent over scenes with Anne and Kong, and then the film basically stops when Kong is captured, and then restarts.

The effect is wearisome BUT it actually helps that by the end of the film, we feel a little worn down by its runtime and pace: it helps the tragedy. And yes, for as long and windy a road it took to get to the top of the Empire State Building, at the end Kong remains a stirring and strikingly tragic tale.

A case could be made that Jackson is our greatest Tragedian: Heavenly Creatures is a tragedy, Lord of the Rings is kind of tragicomic, King Kong is a tragedy, The Lovely Bones is a tragedy, The Hobbit is a tragedy, and both his recent documentaries were tragedies.

Still a fantastic and epic adventure. And I always go in for the extended cut, where you get to more fully explore the horrors of skull island.

My only consistent critiques are 1) that blurry slo-mo that Jackson loves to use, 2) some of the dinosaur stampede is a bit too silly looking, and 3) cut the ice-skating sequence.

The film is long as hell but that’s a *good* thing. It pulls you into the adventure. And it doesn’t start to lose me until we get back to the city.

Of the Kong movies, I would take the 33 and the 76 movies over the 05 movie and it is a huge gap between them.  All I really remember from the movie was how grey everything was, the whole thing was just bland.

It’s so over the top in every way: Three hours, exhausting, extended fight scenes, Jack Black … too much. Peter Jackson lost the subtleties after LOTRs and stopped making movies, just extended action scenes.

Watched it when I was 9 and it will always be one of the most special experiences in a movie theatre. Maybe the first time I realized the scale and the possibilities cinema could have. The moment with the insects and Serkis fighting those worms with teeth haunted me for years. Unforgettable.

When the movie was originally announced i was on a hype train and followed the official website until movie release night. We had a massive billboard out the front of work for months that generally had crappy typical highway ads on it. They plastered this with the iconic Kong v Trex pose with Ann in the middle. I was pumped!

  


Saw it on release night and loved it. The dino tumbling scene and the bug fight scene were the only two i thought felt a bit long winded. The build up, the Ann introduction, the sea journey and finally seeing the wall. Awesome. Enjoyed the slow burn. Kyle Chandler as Bruce Baxter, funny af.

  


As a '70's kid, campy King Kong was my first remembered big screen movie and it blew me away. Jacksons Kong lived up to that experience as an adult.
